verses.text: When all the nation had completely crossed over the Jordan, Yahweh spoke to Joshua, saying,
“Take twelve men out of the people, a man out of every tribe,

and command them, saying, ‘Take from out of the middle of the Jordan, out of the place where the priests’ feet stood firm, twelve stones, and carry them over with you, and lay them down in the place where you’ll camp tonight.’”
Then Joshua called the twelve men, whom he had prepared of the children of Israel, a man out of every tribe.

Joshua said to them, “Cross before the ark of Yahweh your God into the middle of the Jordan, and each of you pick up a stone and put it on your shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the children of Israel;
that this may be a sign among you, that when your children ask in the future, saying, ‘What do you mean by these stones?’

then you shall tell them, ‘Because the waters of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of Yahweh’s covenant. When it crossed over the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were cut off. These stones shall be for a memorial to the children of Israel forever.’”

The children of Israel did as Joshua commanded, and took up twelve stones out of the middle of the Jordan, as Yahweh spoke to Joshua, according to the number of the tribes of the children of Israel. They carried them over with them to the place where they camped, and laid them down there.
Joshua set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, in the place where the feet of the priests who bore the ark of the covenant stood; and they are there to this day.

For the priests who bore the ark stood in the middle of the Jordan, until everything was finished that Yahweh commanded Joshua to speak to the people, according to all that Moses commanded Joshua; and the people hurried and passed over.
When all the people had completely crossed over, Yahweh’s ark crossed over, with the priests, in the presence of the people.
The children of Reuben, and the children of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, crossed over armed before the children of Israel, as Moses spoke to them.
About forty thousand men, ready and armed for war passed over before Yahweh to battle, to the plains of Jericho.
On that day, Yahweh magnified Joshua in the sight of all Israel; and they feared him, as they feared Moses, all the days of his life.
Yahweh spoke to Joshua, saying,
“Command the priests who bear the ark of the testimony, that they come up out of the Jordan.”
Joshua therefore commanded the priests, saying, “Come up out of the Jordan!”

When the priests who bore the ark of Yahweh’s covenant had come up out of the middle of the Jordan, and the soles of the priests’ feet had been lifted up to the dry ground, the waters of the Jordan returned to their place, and went over all its banks, as before.
The people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and encamped in Gilgal, on the east border of Jericho.
Joshua set up those twelve stones, which they took out of the Jordan, in Gilgal.
He spoke to the children of Israel, saying, “When your children ask their fathers in time to come, saying, ‘What do these stones mean?’
Then you shall let your children know, saying, ‘Israel came over this Jordan on dry land.
For Yahweh your God dried up the waters of the Jordan from before you, until you had crossed over, as Yahweh your God did to the Red Sea, which he dried up from before us, until we had crossed over;
that all the peoples of the earth may know that Yahweh’s hand is mighty; that you may fear Yahweh your God forever.’”

footnotes.content: The nation has stepped onto dry ground—all of them, not just the first. Now Yahweh speaks to Joshua. I notice how often the Lord gives His next instruction after the miracle is *done*, not before. He waits for us to cross over, then calls us to *remember*.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Twelve men—one from each tribe. Already, the Lord is thinking about unity and witness. Not Joshua alone, not a clergy class. The testimony will be carried by *all the people*, one voice per tribe.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan—from where the priests stood firm in the water's heart. What a place to take them from: not the dry banks, but the deepest, most sacred ground. The most dangerous place becomes the source of remembrance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua had already *prepared* these twelve men. Before Yahweh ever spoke, Joshua was thinking ahead, choosing ones he could trust. The Lord honours readiness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Each man bears a stone on his own shoulder—personal, visible, weighty. Not abstract; not someone else's burden. In faith, we each carry our own witness of what Yahweh has done.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The stones are *a sign for you*—first for the generation that crossed. Then for the children who will ask *in time to come*. Yahweh builds memorials not just for today but for questions the future will raise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The simple story—the waters cut off, the people passed, the stones stay forever. Notice how it's *for a memorial to the children of Israel forever*. The Lord doesn't just want us to remember once; He wants remembrance woven into the next generation's blood.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The children of Israel *did as Joshua commanded*. Obedience. They took the stones and carried them—something visible, something *their hands held*. Faith that works.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua also set up twelve stones *in the middle of the Jordan*—a second memorial underwater, out of sight. Only Yahweh sees it. I love that Yahweh's works are not always *for the eyes* of crowds; some are witnessed only in eternity's memory.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The priests stood firm in the Jordan *until everything was finished that Yahweh commanded*. Not one moment before. They bore the weight—literal and spiritual—until it was time to move. Faithfulness means staying in your post until the Lord releases you.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The whole people crossed. Then the *ark* crossed, with the priests. The holy thing came *after* the people were safe—protection, precedence, finality. The Lord closes the door after His people are home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Reuben, Gad, and half-Manasseh crossed armed. They had given their word to Moses; now they keep it. Even in joy and miracle, some remain weapons-ready—not for rebellion, but for the battles ahead that still need fighting.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Forty thousand warriors, armed, ready. The Lord has given them *bodies* for the work—not just spirit, but muscle and will. The Promised Land is not won by miracle alone; it's won by people who are prepared to *fight*.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: On that *day*, Yahweh magnified Joshua in all Israel's sight. After crossing the Jordan with the Lord, the people now *fear* Joshua as they feared Moses. Yahweh's blessing flows from the leader into the people's hearts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh speaks again—now to command the priests to come *up* out of the Jordan. The moment of release. As Moses says, Yahweh does nothing without a word; nothing moves without His say-so.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The priests bear the ark of the *testimony*. It is the Lord's testimony, not Israel's. The priests' first duty is to carry the *word*, the covenant, the very voice of Yahweh.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua commands the priests to come up—Joshua obeys and then *obeys forward*, passing the word down like a relay. Authority is not power hoarded; it's a message passed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The moment the priests' feet touch dry ground—*instantly*—the waters return. Not slowly, not gently. The Lord holds back the flood; the moment His servants step clear, He releases it. Perfect timing, perfect power.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The tenth day of the first month—Passover season approaches. Israel camps at Gilgal, on the *east border of Jericho*. They are now in Canaan, tasting the land, waiting at the edge of the battle they've come to fight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The twelve stones are set up *in Gilgal*—visible, permanent, a physical thing the hand can point to. Not a legend, not a whisper. A *place* where people can gather and *know*.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua speaks to the children of Israel—this is *his* voice now, carrying the Lord's word into the future. He's teaching them how to teach their *own* children. Faith is not mine alone; it's handed down like water from hand to hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Israel came over this Jordan on dry land.' Simple. Not a song, not a theological thesis—just the fact. *This* happened. *We* saw it. *Here* we stand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He links it to the Red Sea—Yahweh's hand at work twice. Not new; *consistent*. The children will learn that their God is faithful *over generations*, not just once. The God who led Abraham's sons out of Egypt leads *them* into Canaan.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo here: 'that all the peoples of the earth may know that Yahweh's hand is mighty.' The stones at Gilgal spoke to Canaan's nations then; now His works still speak to us—not to frighten, but to call us to *fear the Lord your God forever*. Looking back from our own long road, we see Yahweh's hand at work in the same way.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
